lessons.titleZh: 計劃失控而偏離正常進程

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Without a schedule, the project risks going off the rails.

brief.meaningEn: A plan, discussion or activity becomes disorganised or goes seriously wrong.
brief.meaningZh: 計劃、討論或活動變得失序，或嚴重出錯。
brief.grammar: a project/discussion goes off the rails; went in the past; this lesson teaches a failing-process application.
brief.register: Conventional train metaphor. Some contexts use it about unacceptable personal behaviour; this lesson does not infer wrongdoing from a disrupted project.
brief.boundaryZh: 有意識、可行的計劃調整不等於失控；也不只是一項小延誤，更不必有實際鐵路。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要交代何種控制或進度出了問題，不把一切改動說成失敗。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述失序及具體原因，並提出重整步驟。

options.en: The work became disorganised because dependencies and responsibilities were not coordinated.
options.zh: 先後依賴及責任未協調，工作變得失序。

options.en: The teams agreed a workable new order and completed all the required preparations.
options.zh: 兩隊議定可行新次序，完成所有所需準備。

options.en: One team briefly waited, but all essential responsibilities had already been assigned.
options.zh: 一隊短暫等候，但所有重要責任早已分配。

options.en: The tools were assigned clearly, and waiting was part of an agreed plan.
options.zh: 工具分配清楚，等候屬議定計劃一部分。

listening.explanationZh: 兩隊互等工具、重要工作未分配，顯示協調失序；不是已議定的調整、單次短等且分工清楚，或本在計劃中的等候。
listening.en: The exhibition project went off the rails when no one coordinated the installation: two teams waited for the same tools, while essential tasks were left unassigned.
listening.zh: 沒人協調安裝時，展覽項目失了控：兩隊等同一批工具，重要工作卻沒分配。

reply.promptEn: Why did the exhibition project become difficult to control?
reply.promptZh: 展覽項目為甚麼變得難以控制？

options.en: Nobody coordinated the tools or assigned some essential tasks.
options.zh: 沒人協調工具，也沒分配部分重要工作。

options.en: It went off the rails when the installation work was left uncoordinated.
options.zh: 安裝工作沒人協調，令項目失控。

options.en: Two teams needed the same resources without an agreed sequence.
options.zh: 兩隊需同一資源，卻沒議定先後。

options.en: The missing responsibilities and resource conflicts disrupted the work.
options.zh: 責任缺漏及資源衝突，打亂了工作。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均以工具衝突及責任缺漏解釋協調失序；金句把失控結果連到安裝工作未獲協調的原因。

scene.promptZh: 討論原要決定可行行程，後來不停互相打斷、離題，沒有紀錄或結論。哪句貼切？

options.en: The discussion went off the rails instead of producing a workable plan.
options.zh: 討論失了控，沒有產生可行計劃。

options.en: The discussion followed a clear revised agenda and recorded the decisions.
options.zh: 討論依清楚修訂議程進行，記錄了決定。

options.en: The group changed one stop after comparing the options carefully.
options.zh: 小組細比選項後，改了一個停站。

scene.explanationZh: 打斷、離題、無結論，支持失序；有理由的行程調整本身不算失控。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以說計劃 go off the rails？

options.en: Unassigned work and conflicting arrangements repeatedly block the next steps.
options.zh: 未分配工作及衝突安排，反覆阻住下一步。

options.en: A team deliberately revises one stage after checking the impact and agreeing a new schedule.
options.zh: 團隊查清影響、議定新時間表後，有意調整一個階段。

options.en: A discussion loses its purpose as interruptions prevent any decision.
options.zh: 打斷令無法決定，討論失去原來目的。

contrast.explanationZh: 檢視後的有序調整不等於失控；須看進度、協調及目的如何受影響。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說安裝失控，想只把展覽名字換掉，未處理工具衝突及責任缺漏。哪句建議最好？

options.en: The work went off the rails over coordination, so let us assign the missing tasks and agree the tool sequence first.
options.zh: 工作因協調而失控；先分配漏了的任務，議定工具次序吧。

options.en: Choose a new title before checking who will complete the tasks that still have no owner.
options.zh: 先選新標題，再查誰完成仍無人負責的工作。

options.en: Keep both teams waiting for the same tools until one decides independently to change its plan.
options.zh: 讓兩隊繼續等同一工具，直到其中一隊自行改計劃。

dialogue.explanationZh: 回應已知失控原因需分工及協調資源；只改名字或等待別人自行處理，都未解問題。

speaking.en: The project went off the rails when the roles became unclear, so we need to agree the next steps together.
speaking.zh: 角色不清令項目失控，所以我們需一起議定下一步。
speaking.promptZh: 你想指出失序原因，也提出重整。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你重讀自己的短文，發現中段連續加入無關資料，核心問題不再清楚；你想刪離題段落、重建論證次序。用一至兩句英文描述。

examples.en: My argument went off the rails when I added details that did not answer the question. I need to remove the digressions and rebuild the order.
examples.zh: 加入沒回答問題的細節時，我的論證偏離了正常進程。我需刪離題內容，重建次序。

examples.en: The essay has gone off the rails in the middle, so I will return to the main question and decide which paragraphs actually support it.
examples.zh: 短文中段已偏離正常進程，所以我會回到核心問題，決定哪些段落真正支持它。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用無關細節及核心失焦支持論證失序，提出刪改與重建；不要把每項有理由的修訂也叫失控。

takeaways.en: The discussion went off the rails when people stopped listening to one another.
takeaways.zh: 大家不再互聽時，討論失了控。

takeaways.en: Our plan was going off the rails until we clarified the missing responsibilities.
takeaways.zh: 我們的計劃原正失控，直到釐清缺漏責任。

lessons.titleEn: throw a spanner in the works
lessons.titleZh: 突然打亂原本順利的計劃

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A rail strike could throw a spanner in the works.
sources.expression: throw a spanner in the works

brief.meaningEn: Cause a problem that prevents a plan from proceeding smoothly.
brief.meaningZh: 造成問題，令計劃不能按原定方式順利進行。
brief.grammar: throw a spanner in/into the works; threw/thrown are irregular past forms; the subject may be an event, not a person.
brief.register: Informal British idiom; the source in form is retained, with the common into variant recognised.
brief.boundaryZh: 不必是故意破壞，也不必令事情永遠失敗；要有原計劃及被打亂的具體部分。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是每項普通變化都有足夠影響，需說明障礙如何妨礙順利進行。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述突發干擾，分開事件影響與未證實動機。

options.en: It created a concrete obstacle to the planned object-based lesson.
options.zh: 它為原定圍繞展品的課堂，造成實際障礙。

options.en: It was already included in the visit plan and required no change.
options.zh: 閉館早已列入參觀計劃，無需改動。

options.en: The group had planned a document-only lesson and never needed to see the objects.
options.zh: 小組原計劃只用文件上課，不需看展品。

options.en: It proves that someone closed the museum specifically to harm this group.
options.zh: 它證明有人專為傷害這小組而閉館。

listening.explanationZh: 無法看課堂核心展品，是實際干擾；不是早已預計閉館、原本只用文件，也無故意針對小組的證據。
listening.en: The museum’s unexpected closure threw a spanner in the works of our visit, because the group could no longer see the objects the lesson was built around.
listening.zh: 博物館意外閉館，打亂了參觀計劃，因為小組無法再看課堂圍繞的展品。

reply.promptEn: Why did the unexpected museum closure disrupt your visit?
reply.promptZh: 博物館意外閉館，為甚麼打亂了你們的參觀？

options.en: We could no longer see the objects the lesson needed.
options.zh: 我們無法再看課堂所需展品。

options.en: It threw a spanner in the works because the planned activity depended on those objects.
options.zh: 原定活動依靠那些展品，所以閉館打亂了計劃。

options.en: Our original learning activity could not go ahead in the way we had arranged.
options.zh: 原定學習活動無法按已安排方式進行。

options.en: We needed an alternative rather than following the unchanged visit plan.
options.zh: 我們需替代安排，不能照原參觀計劃不改。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均解釋展品不可用的障礙；金句不指控未證實的故意破壞。

scene.promptZh: 表演前一天，原定場地通知舞台不能用，你們需改排練安排。哪句貼切？

options.en: The unavailable stage threw a spanner in the works.
options.zh: 舞台不能用，打亂了計劃。

options.en: The stage was available exactly as agreed, so no part of the rehearsal needed changing.
options.zh: 舞台完全按議定可用，排練無需改動。

options.en: The planned stage work can continue unchanged by using only the rehearsal notes.
options.zh: 只用排練筆記，原定舞台工作便可完全照舊。

scene.explanationZh: 核心舞台不能用，迫使改排練安排；不是舞台照常可用，也不能假定筆記已代替實際舞台。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜只憑 throw a spanner in the works 得出？

options.en: A problem interrupts the smooth progress of a plan.
options.zh: 問題打斷計劃順利進行。

options.en: A person must have deliberately intended to sabotage the plan.
options.zh: 必定有人故意想破壞計劃。

options.en: The group may need to adjust the original arrangement.
options.zh: 小組可能需調整原安排。

contrast.explanationZh: 事件也可作主語，片語描述影響，不自行確立動機。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴見閉館打亂參觀，就想在紀錄寫成「館方故意針對我們」；未有動機證據。哪句較準確？

options.en: The closure threw a spanner in the works, but record its effect separately from any claim about the museum’s intentions.
options.zh: 閉館打亂計劃，但記錄影響時，應與對館方動機的說法分開。

options.en: Write that the closure targeted our group before asking why the building was unavailable.
options.zh: 未問大樓為何不能用，就寫閉館針對我們。

options.en: Remove the closure from the record because its cause is uncertain, even though the activity had to change.
options.zh: 即使活動須改，也因閉館原因未明，就從紀錄刪掉閉館影響。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可如實記干擾，也保留原因未知；不是猜動機，或因原因未知就抹去實際影響。

speaking.en: The change threw a spanner in the works, so we need a new arrangement without guessing anyone’s intentions.
speaking.zh: 改變打亂計劃，所以我們需新安排，不猜別人動機。
speaking.promptZh: 你想區分已知影響與未知原因。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你研究一段地方歷史，原計劃引用某份手稿，但檔案室通知它暫時不供查閱；你需找其他可靠紀錄，不假定有人阻撓。用一至兩句英文描述。

examples.en: The temporary restriction threw a spanner in the works of my research, because I had planned to consult that manuscript. I will look for other reliable records.
examples.zh: 暫時查閱限制打亂了研究，因為我原計劃查看那份手稿。我會找其他可靠紀錄。

examples.en: Losing access to the manuscript has thrown a spanner in the works, so I need to rethink the evidence I can actually examine.
examples.zh: 無法查閱手稿，打亂了計劃，所以我需重想實際可檢視的證據。

writing.selfCheckZh: 說明原定手稿證據不可查的具體干擾，提出可靠替代資料；不因計劃受阻就推斷有人故意阻撓。

takeaways.en: The last-minute venue change threw a spanner in the works.
takeaways.zh: 最後一刻改場地，打亂了計劃。

takeaways.en: An unavailable document can throw a spanner in the works of a research plan.
takeaways.zh: 一份無法查閱的文件，可打亂研究計劃。

sources.sentence: He misses meetings because he cannot be bothered to check the time.

brief.meaningEn: Do not want to spend the time or effort needed to do something.
brief.meaningZh: 不想花所需時間或心力做某事。
brief.grammar: cannot/can’t be bothered to + verb; couldn’t be bothered in a past account; do not confuse it with being unable to access something.
brief.register: Informal, especially common in British English; may sound dismissive when directed at a shared responsibility.
brief.boundaryZh: 表達不願費心，不一定代表沒有能力；反過來，沒完成事情本身也不能證明是不願。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要看當事人明說的意願及限制，不能把技術或時間障礙直接稱懶得做。
brief.outcomeZh: 能分清不願投入與不能完成，並顧及對話語氣。

listening.promptZh: 說話者為甚麼沒標照片？

options.en: The speaker does not want to spend the effort tonight, despite knowing how.
options.zh: 說話者雖懂怎做，今晚卻不想花心力。

options.en: The speaker has never learnt the labelling method.
options.zh: 說話者從未學過標示方法。

options.en: The files cannot be opened, so the speaker has no access to the photos.
options.zh: 檔案開不到，所以說話者無法取用照片。

options.en: The speaker has already finished sorting and labelling every photo.
options.zh: 說話者已把每張照片分類、標好。

listening.explanationZh: I know how 與不想今晚做對比，指意願，不是技能、權限或已完成。
listening.en: I know how to label the photos, but I cannot be bothered to do it tonight; I would rather leave the sorting for tomorrow.
listening.zh: 我知道怎樣標照片，但今晚懶得做；我寧願把分類留待明天。

reply.promptEn: Why are you leaving the photo sorting until tomorrow when you know how to do it?
reply.promptZh: 你知道怎樣分類照片，為甚麼仍留待明天？

options.en: I do not feel like spending the effort on it tonight.
options.zh: 我今晚不想花心力做。

options.en: I cannot be bothered to label them tonight.
options.zh: 我今晚懶得替它們加標示。

options.en: I would rather put the sorting aside for this evening.
options.zh: 我今晚寧願先擱下分類。

options.en: It is something I can do, but I do not want to tackle it now.
options.zh: 我有能力做，但現在不想處理。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都坦白說今晚不想投入，並非方法不懂或檔案不可用。

scene.promptZh: 角色會使用已開啟的表格，也有空，卻明說「我就是不想花心力填」，把它留待明天。哪句準確？

options.en: She cannot be bothered to fill it in now.
options.zh: 她現在懶得填。

options.en: She cannot open the form and therefore has no way to fill it in.
options.zh: 她開不到表格，所以無法填。

options.en: She has already completed the form but is waiting to send it.
options.zh: 她已填好表格，只等傳送。

scene.explanationZh: 明說不想費心，才支持意願用法，不是權限或等待提交。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以單獨支持 cannot be bothered？

options.en: Someone says they could do the task but do not want to spend the effort.
options.zh: 某人說有能力做，但不想花心力。

options.en: Someone cannot access a required file, and nothing is said about willingness.
options.zh: 某人取不到所需檔案，沒有說意願如何。

options.en: Someone openly chooses not to tackle a task because it feels like too much effort.
options.zh: 某人公開選擇不做，因覺要花太多心力。

contrast.explanationZh: 沒有完成或取不到檔案，不等於不願費心；需意願線索。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴因檔案權限未開而未能分類，你想如實記原因。朋友卻建議寫 cannot be bothered。哪句回應最好？

options.en: We do not know that she cannot be bothered; the known problem is access to the file.
options.zh: 我們不知道她是否懶得做；已知問題是檔案取用權限。

options.en: Describe the unfinished task as unwillingness before checking whether she could open the file.
options.zh: 未查她能否開檔，就把未完工作說成不願做。

options.en: Record the access problem as fixed simply because she already knows the sorting method.
options.zh: 只因她已懂分類方法，就記作權限問題已解。

dialogue.explanationZh: 區分意願、技能及取用條件；懂方法不會自動取得權限，未完成也不能證明懶得做。

speaking.en: I cannot be bothered to sort the photos tonight, but that is different from not knowing how.
speaking.zh: 我今晚懶得分類照片，但這與不懂怎做不同。
speaking.promptZh: 你想坦白意願，也分開能力。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在對話中回顧昨天：本來打算修補自己的舊筆袋，材料及方法都有，最後只是覺得麻煩而不想做；今天想坦白說明這個選擇。用一至兩句英文描述。

examples.en: I could not be bothered to mend the pencil case yesterday, even though I had the materials and knew how. I simply did not want to make the effort then.
examples.zh: 昨天我懶得修筆袋，即使有材料、也懂怎修。當時我只是不想花心力。

examples.en: I couldn’t be bothered to repair it yesterday; the issue was my willingness, not missing supplies or instructions.
examples.zh: 昨天我懶得修；問題是不願投入，不是缺用品或指引。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用過去式描述自己明說的選擇，保留材料、方法齊備的條件，不從他人未做就猜動機。

takeaways.en: I can cook, but I cannot be bothered to make a complicated meal tonight.
takeaways.zh: 我會煮飯，但今晚懶得做複雜一餐。

takeaways.en: He admitted that he couldn’t be bothered to check the list again.
takeaways.zh: 他承認自己懶得再查清單。

sources.sentence: Arriving five minutes before check-in closes is cutting it fine.

brief.meaningEn: Leave only a very small margin of time before a deadline or required arrival.
brief.meaningZh: 距限期或所需到達時間，只留下很少時間餘裕。
brief.grammar: be cutting it fine; cut it fine in present or past; this lesson focuses on time margins.
brief.register: Informal, especially familiar in British English; not necessarily already late.
brief.boundaryZh: 仍可能趕及，卻幾乎沒有應付延誤的餘裕；不能只按分鐘數，還需看要做的事。
brief.misconceptionZh: 與準時或已遲到有別，重點是可用緩衝很少。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出限期前的微小緩衝及其風險，不直接斷言已錯過。

listening.promptZh: 說話者怎樣看這個到達時間？

options.en: It may still be in time, but there is very little room for delay.
options.zh: 仍可能趕及，但幾乎沒延誤餘裕。

options.en: They have already missed the closing time before setting out.
options.zh: 他們未出發，已錯過關門時間。

options.en: There is a large buffer for queuing and unexpected delays.
options.zh: 排隊及意外延誤都有大量緩衝。

options.en: The closing time has been extended, so the queue no longer matters.
options.zh: 關門時間已延長，所以排隊不再重要。

listening.explanationZh: 預計前兩分鐘仍可能趕及；even a short queue 交代缺乏緩衝，而非已遲或已延長。
listening.en: We expect to arrive two minutes before the hall doors close, so we are cutting it fine: even a short queue could leave us outside.
listening.zh: 我們預計會堂關門前兩分鐘到，所以時間很緊：即使短隊，也可能令我們進不去。

reply.promptEn: Why are you concerned about arriving two minutes before the doors close?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼你擔心關門前兩分鐘才到？

options.en: There is almost no time for a queue or a small delay.
options.zh: 幾乎沒時間應付排隊或小延誤。

options.en: We are cutting it fine because the spare time is so short.
options.zh: 時間餘裕太少，所以我們時間很緊。

options.en: A minor interruption could make us miss entry.
options.zh: 小打斷也可能令我們趕不及入場。

options.en: The arrival estimate leaves very little buffer before closing.
options.zh: 預計到達時間，離關門只有很少緩衝。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋微小餘裕，而非只把準時與遲到二分。

scene.promptZh: 報告八時交，你七時五十九分才開始上傳，檔案還未傳完；不是已確定超時。哪句貼切？

options.en: I am cutting it fine with the upload.
options.zh: 這次上傳，我留的時間餘裕很少。

options.en: I have allowed plenty of time for a failed upload and another attempt.
options.zh: 我已預留大量時間應付傳送失敗及再試。

options.en: The deadline has definitely passed before the upload begins.
options.zh: 上傳開始前，限期肯定已過。

scene.explanationZh: 只剩一分鐘且未傳完，支持餘裕很小；題目未說限期已過。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 cutting it fine？

options.en: An arrival plan leaves little room for a normal queue.
options.zh: 到達計劃幾乎沒留排一般隊伍的時間。

options.en: A tested submission is completed well before the deadline, with time for another attempt if needed.
options.zh: 已測試的提交早於限期完成，若需再試也有時間。

options.en: The remaining time is only just enough if every stage runs smoothly.
options.zh: 只有每階段都順利，剩餘時間才剛好夠。

contrast.explanationZh: 有足夠再試緩衝，與時間只勉強夠不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴覺得前一分鐘開始上傳就算準時，不用查傳送需時；你們還可以早點開始。哪句建議最好？

options.en: We would be cutting it fine, so let us check the upload time and start with a reasonable buffer.
options.zh: 那會只剩很少餘裕；查上傳需時，預留合理緩衝開始吧。

options.en: Use the click on upload as proof that the full file has reached the system before the deadline.
options.zh: 按下上傳，就當整份檔案已在限期前到系統。

options.en: Wait until the last minute before testing whether the file can be sent.
options.zh: 等最後一分鐘，才試檔案能否傳送。

dialogue.explanationZh: 開始上傳與完成不同；有時間可先查與留緩衝，不能把按鈕動作當完成。

speaking.en: We are cutting it fine, so I would rather leave a little more time for the steps we still need to complete.
speaking.zh: 我們時間餘裕很少，所以我寧願多留一點時間完成餘下步驟。
speaking.promptZh: 你想指出微小緩衝，而不是直接說已遲到。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你借用錄音室兩小時，卻把整段時間排滿錄製，最後只剩兩分鐘儲存、核對檔案及交還器材；你還未超時，想重排最後部分留緩衝。用一至兩句英文描述。

examples.en: We are cutting it fine with only two minutes to save the files and return the equipment. We should shorten the final take and leave a proper handover buffer.
examples.zh: 只剩兩分鐘存檔及交還器材，我們時間餘裕很少。我們應縮短最後錄製，留足交接緩衝。

examples.en: We are cutting it fine at the end of the session, so I want time to check the saved recording before the room booking finishes.
examples.zh: 這節最後，我們時間餘裕很少，所以我想在租用時段結束前，留時間核對已存錄音。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把最後存檔、核對及交還步驟所需時間算進去；時間很緊不等於已超時，也不只看錄製有否準時停止。

takeaways.en: We cut it fine and reached the room just before the talk began.
takeaways.zh: 我們時間抓得很緊，講座開始前才剛到房間。

takeaways.en: Starting the final check so late is cutting it fine.
takeaways.zh: 那麼晚才開始最後核對，時間餘裕很少。

sources.sentence: One delayed bus can throw everything off.

brief.meaningEn: Disrupt the connected parts of a plan or schedule.
brief.meaningZh: 打亂計劃或時間表內互相連接的部分。
brief.grammar: a delay can throw everything off; threw/thrown are irregular; everything refers to the relevant arrangement, not literally all existence.
brief.register: Common throw off phrasal-verb application to a connected plan.
brief.boundaryZh: 不一定每個無關活動都受影響，也不表示永遠無法重整；要指出連鎖關係。
brief.misconceptionZh: 一項變動可能有廣泛影響，但需有相連步驟，不能只見改動就說一切全毀。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述安排的連鎖失準並評估應調整的部分。

options.en: The connected bookings and work periods affected by the late start.
options.zh: 受遲開始影響的相連預訂及工作時段。

options.en: Every activity in the city, including those unrelated to the interview.
options.zh: 全城每項活動，包括與訪問無關的。

options.en: Only the interview’s starting time moved; the room, translator and editing slots stayed as booked.
options.zh: 只有訪問開始時間改，房間、翻譯及編輯時段都維持預訂。

options.en: The room booking changed, but the translator’s next appointment and the editing slot were unaffected.
options.zh: 房間預訂改了，但翻譯下一約見及編輯時段未受影響。

listening.explanationZh: 冒號後列明房間預訂、翻譯下一約見及編輯時段都需重排；不是只開始時間改或只房間改，everything也不擴至無關全城活動。
listening.en: The interview started half an hour late and threw everything off: the room booking, the translator’s next appointment and our editing slot all had to be rearranged.
listening.zh: 訪問遲半小時開始，打亂了整體安排：房間預訂、翻譯下一個約見及我們的編輯時段都需重排。

reply.promptEn: Why did the late interview start require several arrangements to change?
reply.promptZh: 訪問遲開始，為甚麼令幾項安排都要改？

options.en: The room, translator and editing periods were connected in the schedule.
options.zh: 房間、翻譯及編輯時段在時間表內相連。

options.en: It threw everything off because later bookings depended on the interview finishing on time.
options.zh: 後續預訂依靠訪問準時結束，所以它打亂了整體安排。

options.en: The delay pushed against the next commitments rather than staying within spare time.
options.zh: 延誤碰上後續承諾，而非仍在空餘時段內。

options.en: We needed to coordinate the affected people instead of adjusting just one isolated note.
options.zh: 我們需協調受影響的人，而非只改一則獨立筆記。

reply.explanationZh: 四句皆交代相連時段為何受影響，金句也給實際原因。

scene.promptZh: 烘焙課首段準備遲了，之後的焗爐共用、試吃及清場時段互相擠壓，都需調整。哪句合適？

options.en: The delayed preparation threw everything off in the lesson schedule.
options.zh: 準備延誤，打亂了課堂整體時間表。

options.en: The delay fitted entirely within spare time and affected no later stage.
options.zh: 延誤完全落在空餘時間內，沒影響之後階段。

options.en: Only the preparation time changed; the shared oven, tasting and clearing periods stayed as originally planned.
options.zh: 只有準備時間改；共用焗爐、試吃及清場仍照原計劃。

scene.explanationZh: 延誤擠壓焗爐共用、試吃及清場，需連鎖調整；不是全在空餘時間內，也非只有準備時段改。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜只憑 throw everything off 得出？

options.en: Several connected arrangements may need to be reconsidered.
options.zh: 幾項相連安排可能需重想。

options.en: Every unrelated plan is necessarily ruined permanently.
options.zh: 每項無關計劃必定永久毀掉。

options.en: Context identifies the scope of everything.
options.zh: 情境界定 everything 的範圍。

contrast.explanationZh: everything 由當前安排界定；受打亂也不等於永久無法重整。

dialogue.promptZh: 訪問延誤後，同伴只想改房間紀錄，沒有通知翻譯及編輯。你已知三段時間互相影響。哪句建議最好？

options.en: The delay threw everything off, so let us check the connected bookings and contact everyone affected.
options.zh: 延誤打亂整體安排；查相連預訂，聯絡所有受影響的人吧。

options.en: Change only the room record and assume the translator’s next appointment can remain untouched.
options.zh: 只改房間紀錄，假定翻譯下一個約見不需處理。

options.en: Move the editing slot first without checking whether the interview and translator can fit the new time.
options.zh: 未查訪問及翻譯能否配合新時間，就先移編輯時段。

dialogue.explanationZh: 已知相連就需協調整體，不能只改一段或先移後續而未查配合。

speaking.en: The delay threw everything off, but we can identify the affected stages and agree a revised order.
speaking.zh: 延誤打亂整體安排，但我們可找出受影響階段，議定新次序。
speaking.promptZh: 你想交代連鎖影響，也保留可重整的下一步。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你編排一份手工藝說明冊，早期照片標籤編錯，後面圖文配對及交叉參照都受影響；你想先找出相連頁面再修正。用一至兩句英文描述。

examples.en: The wrong photo labels threw everything off in the guide, including the captions and cross-references. I need to trace the affected pages before correcting them.
examples.zh: 照片標籤錯誤，打亂說明冊整體編排，包括圖說及交叉參照。我需先追查受影響頁面，再修正。

examples.en: One labelling error has thrown everything off because several instructions refer to the same pictures. I will check those links rather than change a single caption alone.
examples.zh: 一個標籤錯誤打亂整體，因為幾項指示引用同一照片。我會核對那些連繫，而非只改一項圖說。

writing.selfCheckZh: 說明標籤如何影響多頁圖文及參照，讓 everything 有清楚範圍；不是不查就斷言所有內容永久無用。

takeaways.en: The late delivery threw everything off in our preparation schedule.
takeaways.zh: 延遲送貨，打亂了準備時間表。

takeaways.en: One wrong reference can throw everything off in a set of linked instructions.
takeaways.zh: 一個錯誤參照，可打亂一套相連指示。

sources.sentence: An early warning helped save the day.

brief.meaningEn: Prevent a likely failure or rescue a difficult situation.
brief.meaningZh: 避免本來很可能發生的失敗，或挽救困難局面。
brief.grammar: save/saved the day; an action, resource or person can be the subject.
brief.register: Conventional approving rescue idiom, often at a critical point; not necessarily the final second or a literal whole day.
brief.boundaryZh: 需要有原本的困難及扭轉作用，不只是一般方便；也不保證所有後續問題都消失。
brief.misconceptionZh: 功勞可來自事前準備，也不一定是一位英雄獨力完成。
brief.outcomeZh: 能交代原本風險、關鍵補救及尚存工作。

listening.promptZh: 備用線有甚麼關鍵作用？

options.en: It solved the connection problem that threatened the demonstration.
options.zh: 它解決威脅示範的連接問題。

options.en: It improved the image slightly, but the planned display was already working before it arrived.
options.zh: 它令畫面稍好，但到來前原定顯示已能運作。

options.en: It allowed a different activity to replace the demonstration, rather than restoring the planned one.
options.zh: 它讓另一活動取代示範，而非恢復原定示範。

options.en: It arrived after the demonstration had been cancelled and made no difference to that outcome.
options.zh: 它在示範取消後才到，沒有改變結果。

listening.explanationZh: 原連接故障會妨礙示範，備用線令原定示範得以繼續，是挽救；不是稍改原已可用的畫面、改做另一活動，或取消後才到。
listening.en: The display would not connect to our laptop, but a volunteer’s spare cable saved the day and let the planned demonstration go ahead.
listening.zh: 顯示器連不到手提電腦，但義工的備用線挽救了局面，讓原定示範得以進行。

reply.promptEn: Why were you so grateful for the volunteer’s spare cable?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼那麼感謝義工的備用線？

options.en: It fixed the connection problem that was stopping the demonstration.
options.zh: 它修好妨礙示範的連接問題。

options.en: It saved the day by allowing the planned demonstration to go ahead.
options.zh: 它讓原定示範得以進行，挽救了局面。

options.en: We could show the material after thinking we might have to cancel that part.
options.zh: 原以為可能取消那部分，後來卻能展示材料。

options.en: The spare was the practical solution we needed at that critical point.
options.zh: 備用品是那個關鍵時刻所需的實際解決。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以連接故障獲解，說明感謝備用線的理由；金句肯定它在關鍵時刻讓原定示範得以繼續。

scene.promptZh: 球隊快要落敗，最後階段一個入球讓它扳平並保住繼續比賽的機會。哪句可用來讚賞這次扭轉？

options.en: The late goal saved the day for the team.
options.zh: 較後的入球為球隊挽救局面。

options.en: The team had already secured its place before the late goal.
options.zh: 較後入球前，球隊已確保晉級位置。

options.en: The goal improved the score but left the team without any chance to continue.
options.zh: 入球改善比數，但球隊仍無任何繼續比賽的機會。

scene.explanationZh: 入球扳平、保住繼續機會，扭轉眼前敗局；不是此前已確保晉級，或入球後仍無機會。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 saved the day？

options.en: A backup restores the essential function needed to avoid a likely failure.
options.zh: 備用安排恢復必要功能，避免很可能發生的失敗。

options.en: A pleasant decoration is added, with no difficult situation or threatened failure described.
options.zh: 添了好看裝飾，沒有描述困難局面或失敗風險。

options.en: A clarification prevents a decision based on a serious misunderstanding.
options.zh: 一項澄清，避免因嚴重誤會作決定。

contrast.explanationZh: 普通增添裝飾本身不一定達挽救程度，要交代困難及實際扭轉。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說備用線挽救了示範，便想刪掉接下來仍需做的內容講解。哪句較好？

options.en: The cable saved the day by restoring the display, but we still need to explain the material clearly.
options.zh: 線路恢復顯示、挽救局面，但我們仍需清楚講解材料。

options.en: Use the working display as evidence that the audience already understands the content.
options.zh: 把顯示器運作，當觀眾已理解內容的證據。

options.en: Skip the explanation and move straight to questions on details that have not yet been presented.
options.zh: 略過講解，直接問尚未呈現的細節。

dialogue.explanationZh: 補救恢復展示條件，不會自動完成講解或觀眾理解。

speaking.en: The backup saved the day, but we still had to do the work it made possible.
speaking.zh: 備用安排挽救了局面，但我們仍需做它讓我們得以完成的工作。
speaking.promptZh: 你想肯定補救，也保留後續投入。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：故事中的評審誤以為小組計劃漏了主要成本，差點否決；一位組員清楚指出原表格哪裏已計入，評審因此按正確資料繼續考慮。用一至兩句英文說明這項澄清的作用。

examples.en: Her clarification saved the day by showing where the main cost had already been included. The panel could then assess the plan without that misunderstanding.
examples.zh: 她指出主要成本早已計在哪裏，澄清挽救了局面。評審因此可不受該誤會影響，評估計劃。

examples.en: A clear explanation of the original table saved the day, although the proposal still needed to be judged on its merits.
examples.zh: 清楚解釋原表格，挽救了局面，但提案仍需按本身優劣評審。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把澄清與避免基於誤會的否決連起來，不把獲繼續考慮寫成已獲批准，也不誇大成所有問題都解決。

takeaways.en: The spare copy saved the day when the original could not be opened.
takeaways.zh: 原檔開不到時，備用副本挽救了局面。

takeaways.en: A timely explanation can save the day when a plan is about to be rejected for the wrong reason.
takeaways.zh: 計劃快因錯誤理由遭拒時，及時解釋可挽救局面。

lessons.titleZh: 冒可能惹大麻煩的風險

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Leaving so late is playing with fire.

brief.meaningEn: Take a serious or unwise risk that could cause trouble.
brief.meaningZh: 冒嚴重或不明智的風險，可能惹出麻煩。
brief.grammar: be playing with fire; play/played with fire; name the risk the context establishes.
brief.register: Conventional danger idiom, often a warning; a metaphorical use does not require actual flames.
brief.boundaryZh: 可能出問題不等於問題已發生或必定發生；也不是每項小不便都適合這種較強警告。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要給足夠具體風險，不靠生動說法取代查核。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出具體風險及較穩妥步驟，保留可能而非必然的語氣。

options.en: The action exposes important work to a concrete risk of loss.
options.zh: 行動令重要成果暴露於具體損失風險。

options.en: The file has already been lost, and the sentence confirms recovery is impossible.
options.zh: 檔案已丟失，句子確認無法恢復。

options.en: A verified backup has already removed the described single-copy problem.
options.zh: 已確認備份，消除了所述唯一副本問題。

options.en: The only concern is that the filename looks slightly untidy.
options.zh: 唯一疑慮是檔名看來稍亂。

listening.explanationZh: 唯一副本及可能誤覆寫，支持較強風險警告；could 不表示已失去。
listening.en: Editing the only copy of the group’s final file without checking a backup is playing with fire: one accidental overwrite could lose work we cannot easily recreate.
listening.zh: 未查備份就改全組最後檔案的唯一副本，是冒可能惹大麻煩的風險：一次誤覆寫，可能失去難重做的成果。

reply.promptEn: Why do you want to check a backup before editing that final file?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼想先查備份，再改最後檔案？

options.en: It is the only copy, and an accidental overwrite could lose important work.
options.zh: 它是唯一副本，誤覆寫可能失去重要成果。

options.en: We would be playing with fire if we risked that work without checking another copy.
options.zh: 若沒查另一副本就冒險處理成果，我們是在冒可能惹大麻煩的風險。

options.en: The cost of a mistake could be much more than a small delay.
options.zh: 出錯代價可能遠超小延誤。

options.en: I want to reduce the chance of losing work that would be hard to recreate.
options.zh: 我想減少失去難重做成果的機會。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋已知唯一副本風險；金句用警告比喻，不宣稱出事必然。

scene.promptZh: 你要刊出受訪者一句影響名譽的話，卻還不確定引文是否抄對，朋友想直接發出。哪句可警告這種具體風險？

options.en: Publishing the unchecked quotation would be playing with fire.
options.zh: 刊出未核對引文，會是在冒可能惹大麻煩的風險。

options.en: The quotation has been fully checked, so there is no unresolved accuracy question in this case.
options.zh: 引文已完全核對，所以此處沒有未解準確疑問。

options.en: The editor should treat the uncertain words as a confirmed direct quotation because they sound plausible.
options.zh: 編輯應因未確定的話聽來合理，就當已確認的直接引文。

scene.explanationZh: 關鍵引文未核對便急刊，可能影響名譽，支持風險警告；不是已查清，也不能只因聽來合理就當原話。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜由 playing with fire 得出？

options.en: The speaker regards the action as exposing someone to serious trouble.
options.zh: 說話者認為行動令人面對嚴重麻煩風險。

options.en: The bad outcome has definitely happened already.
options.zh: 壞結果肯定已經發生。

options.en: The warning should be understood using the described circumstances.
options.zh: 應按所述情況理解警告。

contrast.explanationZh: 風險表示可能，不是宣告結果已發生；仍需看具體條件。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說檔案還沒損失，所以不用查備份；你知道目前只有一份。哪句回應最好？

options.en: We would be playing with fire because the loss could happen during editing; check a usable copy before relying on the current one alone.
options.zh: 損失可能在編輯中發生，所以那是在冒嚴重風險；只依現有檔案前，先查可用副本。

options.en: Treat the absence of a past mistake as enough evidence that the only copy cannot be overwritten.
options.zh: 把從前沒出錯，當唯一副本不會被覆寫的足夠證據。

options.en: Rename the only file and assume that gives us a separate recoverable copy.
options.zh: 替唯一檔案改名，便假定有另一份可恢復副本。

dialogue.explanationZh: 沒發生不等於不可能；改名也不等於有獨立副本。

speaking.en: We are playing with fire if we ignore that known risk just because nothing has gone wrong yet.
speaking.zh: 不能只因還沒出事，就忽略已知風險；那是在冒可能惹大麻煩的風險。
speaking.promptZh: 你想區分目前沒事與沒有風險。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：故事中的小組想宣布免費工作坊名額，但贊助只在口頭初談，尚未確認能否負擔；若先作承諾，之後可能取消，令參加者失望。用一至兩句英文指出這項風險，並提出先核實支援。

examples.en: We would be playing with fire by promising free places before the sponsor confirms the support. Let us check the commitment before inviting people.
examples.zh: 贊助者確認支援前，就承諾免費名額，是冒可能惹大麻煩的風險。邀請大家前，先核實承諾吧。

examples.en: Announcing a free workshop on the basis of an informal conversation is playing with fire. We could disappoint the participants if the support does not arrive.
examples.zh: 只憑非正式對話就宣布免費工作坊，是冒可能惹大麻煩的風險。若支援未到，我們可能令參加者失望。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把未確認贊助與先承諾免費名額的落差，連到可能取消及令參加者失望；提出先核實，不把可能風險寫成已發生。

takeaways.en: You are playing with fire by making a promise before checking whether you can keep it.
takeaways.zh: 未查能否履行就承諾，是冒可能惹麻煩的風險。

takeaways.en: The editor warned that publishing an unchecked claim would be playing with fire.
takeaways.zh: 編輯警告，刊出未核對說法，是冒可能惹大麻煩的風險。

sources.sentence: After lunch, I can settle down and read.

brief.meaningEn: Become calmer and ready to give attention to an activity.
brief.meaningZh: 變得較平靜，準備把注意放到一項活動。
brief.grammar: settle down to + noun/-ing, or settle down to do something; settled and settling; this lesson focuses on calming/focusing, not starting a settled home life.
brief.register: Common phrasal verb; context chooses among its different dictionary senses.
brief.boundaryZh: 不一定完全無聲或睡着，也不只等於坐下；要有心情及注意安定的變化。
brief.misconceptionZh: 安定後可繼續積極參與，不表示已完成工作或永久無壓力。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述由分心轉向專注，也以合適語氣請人準備聽。

listening.promptZh: settled down 在此表示甚麼？

options.en: The speaker became ready to focus on reading after the discussion.
options.zh: 討論後，說話者準備好專注閱讀。

options.en: The speaker finished reading before the group discussion began.
options.zh: 小組討論未開始，說話者已讀完。

options.en: The speaker continued chatting and did not turn attention to the passage.
options.zh: 說話者繼續聊天，沒有把注意轉到文章。

options.en: The speaker decided to move home permanently, rather than begin reading.
options.zh: 說話者決定永久搬家，而非開始閱讀。

listening.explanationZh: to read 指向接下來的專注活動；不是已讀完或另個定居意思。
listening.en: After the lively group discussion, I put the notes in order and settled down to read the passage carefully.
listening.zh: 熱烈小組討論後，我整理筆記，安定下來細讀文章。

reply.promptEn: What did you do after the lively discussion?
reply.promptZh: 熱烈討論後，你做了甚麼？

options.en: I organised the notes and began reading carefully.
options.zh: 我整理筆記，開始細讀。

options.en: I settled down to read the passage.
options.zh: 我安定下來讀文章。

options.en: I turned from the group conversation to a quieter individual task.
options.zh: 我從小組交談轉到較平靜的個人工作。

options.en: I got ready to give the text my full attention.
options.zh: 我準備把全部注意放在文章。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述轉向閱讀專注，不表示只是坐下或已完成。

scene.promptZh: 活動開始時同學仍興奮交談，後來收好物品、注意老師，準備聽首項指示。哪句貼切？

options.en: The students settled down and prepared to listen.
options.zh: 同學安定下來，準備聽。

options.en: The students sat down but continued ignoring the instructions in an equally noisy conversation.
options.zh: 同學坐下，卻仍同樣吵聊、不理指示。

options.en: The students moved to the next task immediately without waiting for its instructions.
options.zh: 同學沒等下一項指示，就立即轉到下一工作。

scene.explanationZh: 興奮轉為準備聽，是注意安定；仍吵聊或未聽指示便急做下一項，都未顯示這個轉變。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持本課的 settle down？

options.en: Moving from restless conversation to paying attention to the next task.
options.zh: 從躁動聊天轉到注意下一項工作。

options.en: Taking a chair while remaining just as distracted and not ready to engage.
options.zh: 坐上椅子，但仍一樣分心，未準備參與。

options.en: Becoming calm enough to begin a careful read.
options.zh: 平靜到足以開始細讀。

contrast.explanationZh: 單有坐下位置，沒有心情或注意轉變，不足以支持此義。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說「全班已坐着，所以一定 settled down」，但不少人仍沒聽到首項指示。哪句較準確？

options.en: Sitting down is not the same as settling down; check whether they are ready to listen before giving the next instruction.
options.zh: 坐下不等於安定下來；下一項指示前，先看大家是否準備好聽。

options.en: Treat every occupied chair as evidence that each student heard the first instruction.
options.zh: 把每張有人坐的椅子，當每位同學已聽首項指示的證據。

options.en: Repeat the next instructions faster while the same conversations continue.
options.zh: 同樣聊天仍持續時，更快重複下一項指示。

dialogue.explanationZh: 注意準備與坐姿不同；仍未聽到時加快指示，未處理已知干擾。

speaking.en: Let us settle down and listen to the first instruction before we begin.
speaking.zh: 開始前，讓我們安定下來，聽首項指示。
speaking.promptZh: 你想用共同參與語氣請大家準備聽。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：小說中的孩子剛參加熱鬧慶祝，回房後仍很興奮。家長放低聲音陪她看睡前故事，她漸漸平靜，能跟着情節，但還沒睡着。用一至兩句英文描寫這個轉變。

examples.en: She began to settle down as her father read the bedtime story in a quiet voice. She followed the plot, although she was not asleep yet.
examples.zh: 爸爸輕聲讀睡前故事時，她開始安定下來。她跟着情節，但還沒睡着。

examples.en: After the noisy celebration, the child settled down beside the storybook and listened calmly. Being calmer did not mean she had already fallen asleep.
examples.zh: 熱鬧慶祝後，孩子在故事書旁安定下來，平靜地聽。較平靜不表示已睡着。

writing.selfCheckZh: 描寫從興奮轉為可平靜跟故事的注意變化，保留仍醒着；不把安定等同已入睡。

takeaways.en: After the visitors left, I settled down to finish the chapter.
takeaways.zh: 訪客離開後，我安定下來讀完那章。

takeaways.en: The class settled down when everyone was ready to listen.
takeaways.zh: 大家準備好聽時，全班安定下來。

sources.sentence: A flight connection is a high-stakes deadline.

brief.meaningEn: Involving serious possible consequences, gains or losses.
brief.meaningZh: 涉及可能重大的後果、得益或損失。
brief.grammar: a high-stakes decision/interview/contest; compound adjective, normally before the noun; distinguish stakes from difficulty.
brief.register: Established adjective, not a phrasal verb or an opaque idiom. Stakes can concern opportunities and other valued outcomes, not only money.
brief.boundaryZh: 可能損失重大不等於必定失敗，也不一定題目很難或費用很高；須有情境後果。
brief.misconceptionZh: 同一任務可因人物處境不同而有不同重要性，不只看場面或價格。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體可能後果支持重大得失判斷，分開機率及難度。

options.en: The character faces serious consequences if she loses the opportunity.
options.zh: 角色錯失機會時，面對嚴重後果。

options.en: The interview matters chiefly because its questions are technically difficult.
options.zh: 面試重要，主要因問題技術上很難。

options.en: The sentence confirms that the character has already failed.
options.zh: 句子確認角色已落敗。

options.en: The event is financially important mainly because a large application fee has already been paid.
options.zh: 活動在經濟上重要，主要因已付大筆申請費。

listening.explanationZh: 錯失唯一可能收入來源，是已交代的重大後果；題目難度、已落敗或大筆申請費，都不是句中原因。
listening.en: In the story, the interview is a high-stakes event for the main character because losing the opportunity would mean losing her only possible source of income that month.
listening.zh: 故事中，面試對主角是得失重大的事件，因為錯失機會，就會失去那個月唯一可能收入來源。

reply.promptEn: Why is the interview especially important to the character that month?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼那個月面試對角色特別重要？

options.en: Losing the opportunity would leave her without that possible source of income.
options.zh: 錯失機會，她就沒有那個可能收入來源。

options.en: It is a high-stakes interview because the possible consequences for her are serious.
options.zh: 可能後果對她嚴重，所以面試得失重大。

options.en: The outcome could affect her basic financial position that month.
options.zh: 結果可能影響她那個月的基本經濟處境。

options.en: There is more at risk for her than simply feeling disappointed about one application.
options.zh: 她面對的風險不只一次申請失望。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均說明已交代處境後果，金句不單用重要重複問題。

scene.promptZh: 故事比賽中，資格賽決定球隊能否進唯一決賽席位；友誼賽則沒有選拔後果。哪句有根據？

options.en: The qualifier is a high-stakes match for that team.
options.zh: 資格賽對該隊是得失重大的比賽。

options.en: The qualifier’s importance proves that the team has already lost it.
options.zh: 資格賽重要，證明球隊已輸。

options.en: The friendly match automatically has the same selection consequences as the qualifier.
options.zh: 友誼賽自動有與資格賽相同的選拔後果。

scene.explanationZh: 唯一決賽席位是明確可能得失，不是已輸或每場後果相同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜只憑 high-stakes 得出？

options.en: There are serious possible consequences in the described situation.
options.zh: 所述情況有重大的可能後果。

options.en: Failure is certain and the task must be technically difficult.
options.zh: 失敗必然，而且任務技術上必定很難。

options.en: The stakes may involve an important opportunity rather than a large fee.
options.zh: 得失可涉及重要機會，而非大筆費用。

contrast.explanationZh: 後果大小與失敗必然、技術難度不同，需分開判斷。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友因工作費用不高，就說不可能 high-stakes；故事已說一旦丟失便失去唯一家族記錄。哪句較準確？

options.en: It can be high-stakes because the possible loss matters, even if the fee is small.
options.zh: 即使費用少，可能損失重要，仍可得失重大。

options.en: Judge the stakes from the invoice alone and leave the irreplaceable record out of the assessment.
options.zh: 只按發票判斷得失，不把不可補記錄計入。

options.en: Assume a low price means the original can be replaced, without checking whether another copy exists.
options.zh: 未查有否副本，就假定低價表示原件可替代。

dialogue.explanationZh: 風險涉及珍視成果，不只付費；費用也不證明有替代副本。

speaking.en: It is a high-stakes choice because the possible loss matters, not because the price is high.
speaking.zh: 這項選擇得失重大，因為可能損失重要，而不是價格高。
speaking.promptZh: 你想用具體可能後果解釋 stakes。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：故事中的社區小組要表決是否永久改建唯一的公共花園，改建後附近居民便失去原有聚會空間。會議雖短，決定後果長遠；你想先聽取居民意見。用一至兩句英文描述這項決定。

examples.en: The vote is a high-stakes decision because it could permanently remove the neighbourhood’s only shared garden. We should hear from the residents before deciding.
examples.zh: 這項表決得失重大，因它可能永久移除社區唯一的共用花園。我們應先聽居民意見，再決定。

examples.en: Even a short meeting can involve a high-stakes choice when the future of the community garden depends on it. I want the long-term effects discussed clearly.
examples.zh: 即使會議很短，當社區花園未來取決於它，選擇仍可得失重大。我想清楚討論長遠影響。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把可能失去唯一共用花園的長遠後果，連到重大得失，提出先聽居民；不由會議長短判斷後果，也不預設表決結果。

takeaways.en: The team faces a high-stakes decision about its final place in the competition.
takeaways.zh: 球隊面對關乎最後比賽席位的重大得失決定。

takeaways.en: A small fee can still be part of a high-stakes situation when the possible loss is serious.
takeaways.zh: 可能損失嚴重時，小額費用仍可涉及得失重大情況。

sources.sentence: He strolls in after every meeting has started.

brief.meaningEn: Enter in a slow, relaxed or casual manner.
brief.meaningZh: 以緩慢、輕鬆或隨意的方式走進來。
brief.grammar: stroll in; strolled/strolling in; in gives the direction of entry to the ordinary walking verb stroll.
brief.register: Natural verb + directional adverb. It may sound critical in a lateness context, but the movement itself does not always mean late or disrespectful.
brief.boundaryZh: 要靠時間及情境才知是否遲到；也不能從步伐直接確定內心動機。
brief.misconceptionZh: 原資料會議已開始才進門帶批評，不代表每次 leisurely entry 都不合適。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描寫走入方式，分開動作、到達時間與態度推論。

options.en: A relaxed manner of entering, with lateness established by the separate timing detail.
options.zh: 輕鬆進門方式；遲到則由另外時間細節確立。

options.en: A hurried entrance before the meeting started.
options.zh: 會議開始前，匆忙進門。

options.en: Proof that the speaker knows the exact reason he arrived late.
options.zh: 證明說話者知道他遲到的確切原因。

options.en: Confirmation that he was already seated when the first discussion began.
options.zh: 確認首段討論開始時，他已坐好。

listening.explanationZh: strolled 描寫步伐，ten minutes after 提供遲到；句子未交代原因。
listening.en: He strolled in ten minutes after the meeting began, walking calmly to a chair while the others were already discussing the first item.
listening.zh: 會議開始十分鐘後，他不慌不忙走進來，平靜走向椅子，其他人已討論首項議程。

reply.promptEn: How did he enter after the meeting had already begun?
reply.promptZh: 會議已開始後，他怎樣進門？

options.en: He walked in calmly rather than rushing.
options.zh: 他平靜走進，而非匆忙。

options.en: He strolled in and went to a chair.
options.zh: 他不慌不忙走進，走向椅子。

options.en: His entrance looked relaxed even though the discussion was under way.
options.zh: 即使討論已在進行，他進門看來仍輕鬆。

options.en: He came through the door at an unhurried pace.
options.zh: 他以不匆忙步伐走過門口。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都回答走入方式，不自行指定遲到原因。

scene.promptZh: 下午沒有約定時間，你悠閒逛書店，緩步走入新開展室。哪句可描述動作？

options.en: I strolled in and began looking at the display.
options.zh: 我不慌不忙走進，開始看展示。

options.en: I rushed in because a timed appointment had already begun.
options.zh: 我因定時約見已開始而衝進去。

options.en: The phrase necessarily proves I ignored an agreed starting time.
options.zh: 片語必定證明我沒理議定開始時間。

scene.explanationZh: 沒有約定時段也可輕鬆走入，stroll in 本身不等於遲到。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜只憑 strolled in 得出？

options.en: The arrival was made at an unhurried pace.
options.zh: 進門步伐不匆忙。

options.en: The person must have deliberately disrespected an agreed meeting time.
options.zh: 當事人必定故意不尊重議定會議時間。

options.en: Timing details are needed to establish whether the person was late.
options.zh: 需時間細節才確立當事人有否遲到。

contrast.explanationZh: 動作輕鬆不自行確定遲到或故意態度；需其他情境。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友只讀到 strolled in，未看開始時間就寫「他故意遲到」。哪句回應最好？

options.en: Strolled in describes his manner; check the timing and any stated reason before claiming deliberate lateness.
options.zh: 這描述走入方式；說故意遲到前，先查時間及已交代原因。

options.en: Use his relaxed pace as enough evidence of both the meeting time and his intention.
options.zh: 把輕鬆步伐，當會議時間及動機的足夠證據。

options.en: Delete the separate arrival time because the walking verb already gives all the information needed.
options.zh: 刪去另外到達時間，因走路動詞已提供全部所需資訊。

dialogue.explanationZh: 步伐、時間及原因是不同資料；不能只看動詞就推完全部。

speaking.en: She strolled in at a relaxed pace, but we need the timing to know whether she was late.
speaking.zh: 她以輕鬆步伐走進，但要知道是否遲到，仍需時間資料。
speaking.promptZh: 你想區分走入方式及時間判斷。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫小說人物回到老家的場景，沒有約定聚會時間；他慢慢走進廚房，看見家人正在聊天，想描寫親切而不匆忙的動作，不暗示遲到。用一至兩句英文描述。

examples.en: He strolled in and smiled at the family gathered in the kitchen. There was no fixed arrival time to miss.
examples.zh: 他不慌不忙走進，向聚在廚房的家人微笑。沒有固定到達時間可錯過。

examples.en: She strolled in at an easy pace, enjoying the familiar voices rather than rushing to an appointment.
examples.zh: 她以輕鬆步伐走進，享受熟悉聲音，而非趕赴約見。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用輕鬆步伐及熟悉家人描寫動作，保留沒有固定時間；不要只因 strolled 就加入故意遲到的判斷。

takeaways.en: We strolled in after a leisurely walk and found a table by the window.
takeaways.zh: 悠閒散步後，我們不慌不忙走進，找到窗邊桌子。

takeaways.en: He strolls in calmly, but the story must tell us whether anyone was expecting him earlier.
takeaways.zh: 他平靜走進，但故事需交代是否有人預期他更早到。

brief.meaningEn: It is wiser to take a reasonable precaution than regret not doing so later.
brief.meaningZh: 作合理預防，比之後後悔沒有做較好。
brief.grammar: Better safe than sorry, or it is better to be safe than sorry; the reviewed target recognises both conventional forms.
brief.register: Conventional saying used to justify a precaution when a possible problem matters.
brief.boundaryZh: 不表示風險已發生，也不要求無限增加成本或把一切都避開；預防仍應配合具體情況。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要說明在防甚麼、措施如何有用，不只用諺語取代思考。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用合理預防回應具體可能問題，而非無條件要求最多防備。

options.en: Checking the latest information to reduce the chance of using an outdated entrance.
options.zh: 查最新資料，減少用舊入口的機會。

options.en: Confirming that the group had already gone to the wrong entrance.
options.zh: 確認小組已走到錯入口。

options.en: Ignoring the update because the first message must still be correct.
options.zh: 因最初訊息必定正確，所以忽略更新。

options.en: Cancelling the meeting without checking whether the new location was usable.
options.zh: 未查新地點是否可用，就取消聚會。

listening.explanationZh: 已改過令版本查核有用；預防不表示已走錯，也不需先取消全部活動。
listening.en: The meeting point had changed once already, so I checked the latest message before leaving: better safe than sorry, rather than send the group to the old entrance.
listening.zh: 集合點已改過一次，所以出發前我再查最新訊息：寧可先留意，也不要事後後悔，免得把小組帶到舊入口。

reply.promptEn: Why did you check the latest meeting message before setting out?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼出發前，再查最新集合訊息？

options.en: The location had changed, and I wanted to avoid using the old entrance.
options.zh: 地點改過，我想避免用舊入口。

options.en: Better safe than sorry: a quick check could prevent an unnecessary detour.
options.zh: 寧可先留意也不要後悔：簡短核對可能避免不必要繞路。

options.en: I wanted to make sure the group followed the current arrangement.
options.zh: 我想確保小組跟目前安排。

options.en: The earlier change made it sensible to verify the message rather than rely on memory.
options.zh: 先前改動令再查訊息合理，不只靠記憶。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代具體核對理由；金句不是說已知走錯。

scene.promptZh: 你把重要照片轉存後，想先開幾張確認能看，再收起原裝置，而不是未查便當備份可用。哪句可解釋這項預防？

options.en: Better safe than sorry; let us check that the saved copies open correctly.
options.zh: 寧可先留意也不要後悔；查已存副本能否正常開啟吧。

options.en: The successful copy command alone proves that every saved file is readable.
options.zh: 單憑複製指令成功，就證明每份檔案都可讀。

options.en: Checking means the photographs have definitely already been lost.
options.zh: 核對表示照片肯定已丟失。

scene.explanationZh: 開啟測試對準可用性；不是宣告已丟失，也不只看指令完成。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜由 better safe than sorry 得出？

options.en: A reasonable check can be worth making before a possible problem.
options.zh: 可能問題前，合理核對可值得做。

options.en: Every extra precaution is automatically worthwhile regardless of cost or relevance.
options.zh: 不論成本或相關性，每項額外防備都自動值得。

options.en: The context should show what problem the precaution addresses.
options.zh: 情境應說清預防在處理甚麼問題。

contrast.explanationZh: 諺語支持合理預防，不代表無限增加成本或做無關檢查。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想用諺語叫全組提早半天到場，但場地當時不開；查訊息只需幾分鐘。哪句較合理？

options.en: Better safe than sorry supports checking the current details, not waiting half a day outside a closed venue.
options.zh: 寧可預先留意，支持查目前詳情，不是關門場地外等半天。

options.en: Choose the earliest possible arrival without checking whether the venue can receive anyone then.
options.zh: 不查場地何時接待，就選最早可能到達時間。

options.en: Skip the updated location check because arriving early alone will settle which entrance is correct.
options.zh: 只因早到就會知道正確入口，所以略過地點更新核對。

dialogue.explanationZh: 措施需相關及可行：查詳情可防錯入口，盲目早到不能代替資訊。

speaking.en: Better safe than sorry; I will check the current details before relying on the old plan.
speaking.zh: 寧可預先留意也不要後悔；依舊計劃前，我會查目前詳情。
speaking.promptZh: 你想把預防連到實際資料核對。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你要把手繪展板送到另一校區，先量門口及展板，確認能通過，免得運到才發現太闊。你只想做針對性的準備。用一至兩句英文說明。

examples.en: Better safe than sorry: let us measure the doorway and display board before arranging the delivery. That check could prevent a problem on arrival.
examples.zh: 寧可先留意也不要後悔：安排運送前，先量門口及展板。這項核對可能避免到場出問題。

examples.en: I want to check the board’s dimensions against the entrance before we carry it across town; better safe than sorry.
examples.zh: 把展板搬到城中另一處前，我想對照板的尺寸及入口；寧可先留意也不要後悔。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把量度與展板能否通過入口連起來，說明預防的具體用途，不把合理準備擴大成無限防備。

takeaways.en: Better safe than sorry; check the address before sending the invitation.
takeaways.zh: 寧可先留意也不要後悔；寄邀請前先查地址。

takeaways.en: We tested the saved copy first: better safe than sorry.
takeaways.zh: 我們先測試已存副本：寧可先留意也不要後悔。

brief.meaningEn: Become comfortable and familiar with a new place, situation or routine.
brief.meaningZh: 逐漸熟悉新地方、情況或作息，感到較自在。
brief.grammar: settle in at a new place; give someone time to settle in; settled/settling.
brief.register: Common phrasal verb for adjustment. Unlike this course’s settle-down lesson, the focus here is getting used to a new setting.
brief.boundaryZh: 在場或拿到鑰匙不等於已適應，也不保證完全掌握每項工作；所需時間因人及情況而異。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能只看第一天安靜，就斷言本人已自在或不需支援。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述熟悉過程，並提供有針對性的入門協助。

listening.promptZh: settle in 在這裏的重點是甚麼？

options.en: Becoming familiar and comfortable in a new setting.
options.zh: 在新環境變得熟悉及自在。

options.en: Merely arriving at the door before any adjustment begins.
options.zh: 調整尚未開始前，單是到門口。

options.en: The few days were spent travelling to the school rather than adjusting after arrival.
options.zh: 那幾天用來前往學校，而非抵達後適應。

options.en: Remaining quiet throughout the first day proves they need no orientation.
options.zh: 首天一直安靜，就證明不需入門介紹。

listening.explanationZh: 熟悉布局及求助對象，然後自在參與，是適應過程，不只抵達或安靜。
listening.en: The new students needed a few days to settle in, learning the room layout and whom to ask before they felt comfortable joining the activities.
listening.zh: 新生需幾天適應，熟悉房間布局及可問誰，之後才自在參與活動。

reply.promptEn: Why did the new students need some time before joining comfortably?
reply.promptZh: 新生為甚麼需一些時間，才自在參與？

options.en: They were learning how the unfamiliar place worked.
options.zh: 他們在學習陌生環境如何運作。

options.en: They needed to settle in and learn whom to ask for help.
options.zh: 他們需適應，也學習可向誰求助。

options.en: Understanding the rooms and contacts helped them feel less uncertain.
options.zh: 了解房間及聯絡人，幫他們減少不確定。

options.en: The activities became easier to join once they knew their way around.
options.zh: 熟悉環境後，活動較易參與。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋熟悉新環境的需要，金句給具體求助對象而非只重述。

scene.promptZh: 你剛加入義工中心，經過幾次導覽及與同伴合作後，開始熟悉流程，也敢問問題。哪句貼切？

options.en: I am beginning to settle in at the volunteer centre.
options.zh: 我開始適應義工中心。

options.en: I have only received the address and have not visited or learnt about the place yet.
options.zh: 我只收到地址，尚未到訪或了解那裏。

options.en: I have arrived, but I still cannot locate the main rooms or ask anyone for help comfortably.
options.zh: 我已到達，但仍找不到主要房間，也未能自在向人求助。

scene.explanationZh: 幾次導覽、熟悉流程及自在求助，支持適應中；不是尚未到訪，也不只是到達後仍不熟悉。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以單獨證明某人已 settled in？

options.en: They know the main routine and feel comfortable asking for help.
options.zh: 他們認識主要流程，也自在求助。

options.en: They collected a key but have not yet learnt the new setting or met anyone there.
options.zh: 他們取了鑰匙，但尚未了解新環境，也未見那裏的人。

options.en: They have become familiar with the spaces they use each day.
options.zh: 他們已熟悉每天使用的空間。

contrast.explanationZh: 取得進入條件與熟悉自在不同，要有適應的行為及感受線索。

dialogue.promptZh: 新同伴第一天很安靜，朋友便說他一定已適應，不需任何介紹；他其實還不知道去哪取用品。哪句較好？

options.en: He may still be settling in; show him where the supplies are and ask what else would help.
options.zh: 他可能仍在適應；帶他看用品在哪，問還有甚麼有幫助。

options.en: Use his quietness as evidence that he already knows the supply routine.
options.zh: 把他安靜當已懂取用品流程的證據。

options.en: Give him a larger task before checking whether he knows the basic locations.
options.zh: 未查他是否知基本位置，就給更大工作。

dialogue.explanationZh: 已知不知用品位置，可提供具體介紹；安靜不等於熟悉，更大任務不能代替入門。

speaking.en: I am still settling in, so could you show me where to find the materials?
speaking.zh: 我仍在適應，可否帶我看去哪裏找材料？
speaking.promptZh: 你想坦白熟悉中的狀態並具體求助。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：故事人物剛搬到新社區，慢慢認識上學路、附近店舖及鄰居，感到較自在，但不說所有事已熟透。用一至兩句英文描述這個過程。

examples.en: I am settling in as I learn the school route, visit nearby shops and get to know the neighbours. The area is beginning to feel more familiar.
examples.zh: 熟習上學路、逛附近店舖及認識鄰居時，我正逐漸適應。這區開始感覺較熟悉。

examples.en: She is starting to settle in after the move, although she still has questions about the neighbourhood.
examples.zh: 搬家後，她開始適應，但對社區仍有疑問。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用認識路線、人及日常設施支持逐漸適應，容許仍有疑問；不只說已搬入便斷言完全熟悉。

takeaways.en: The new volunteer is settling in and learning how the centre works.
takeaways.zh: 新義工正適應，了解中心如何運作。

takeaways.en: It took time to settle in after moving to the neighbourhood.
takeaways.zh: 搬到這社區後，適應花了一些時間。

sources.sentence: Guests should find their seat before the ceremony begins.

brief.meaningEn: Locate the place where a person is meant to sit.
brief.meaningZh: 找出一個人應坐的位置。
brief.grammar: find your seat / guests find their seats; found in the past; the possessive identifies the assigned or intended place.
brief.register: Natural event-going collocation, literal rather than idiomatic.
brief.boundaryZh: 找到位置不等於買票、預留位置或已坐下；看見空位也未必是自己的位置。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要用當前座位資料，而非假定上次的位置或最近空椅就是正確。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述按指示找位置，並在資訊不清時詢問。

listening.promptZh: find our seats 交代甚麼？

options.en: They located the places indicated by their ticket details.
options.zh: 他們找到票上資料所指的位置。

options.en: They bought tickets for the first time after entering the row.
options.zh: 他們進了那行後才首次買票。

options.en: They reserved the whole row for a future event rather than locating a place now.
options.zh: 他們為將來活動預留整行，而非現在找位置。

options.en: They chose the nearest empty chairs without consulting the numbers.
options.zh: 他們沒有查號碼，就選最近空椅。

listening.explanationZh: 行數、座號及告示支持找出正確位置；不是購票、另日預留或隨選空椅。
listening.en: The tickets showed row and seat numbers, so we used the signs to find our seats before the performance began.
listening.zh: 票上有行數及座號，所以演出前我們按告示找到自己的位置。

reply.promptEn: How did you know where to sit before the performance?
reply.promptZh: 演出前，你們怎樣知道應坐哪裏？

options.en: We matched the ticket numbers with the row signs.
options.zh: 我們對照票上號碼與行數告示。

options.en: We used the signs to find our seats.
options.zh: 我們按告示找到自己的位置。

options.en: The row and seat details guided us to the right places.
options.zh: 行數及座號資料引我們到正確位置。

options.en: We checked the labels against the numbers printed on our tickets.
options.zh: 我們對照標籤及票上印的號碼。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代按資料定位，不表示只要空椅便對。

scene.promptZh: 午宴桌上有名卡，你先找自己的名字，確認應坐哪裏，還未開始用餐。哪句貼切？

options.en: I found my seat by checking the name cards.
options.zh: 我查看名卡，找到自己的位置。

options.en: I reserved a place by putting my bag on an unlabelled chair.
options.zh: 我把袋放在沒有標示的椅子上，以預留一個位置。

options.en: I took my seat and started lunch before checking the name cards.
options.zh: 我未查名卡，就坐下開始吃午餐。

scene.explanationZh: 先看自己名卡，是找出應坐位置；不是以袋另留座，也不是未查便已坐下用餐。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜只憑 found their seats 得出？

options.en: The people located the places intended for them.
options.zh: 那些人找到預定給他們的位置。

options.en: The people necessarily bought or reserved the tickets at that moment.
options.zh: 那些人必定當時才購買或預留票。

options.en: They may use labels, numbers or an usher’s guidance to locate the places.
options.zh: 他們可用標籤、號碼或接待引導找位置。

contrast.explanationZh: find 在此是定位，購票預留是不同動作，也不等於已坐下。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴拿着有座號的票，想直接坐最近空椅，未核對是否有人預定。哪句建議最好？

options.en: Let us find our seats using the ticket numbers before choosing an empty chair.
options.zh: 選空椅前，先按票上號碼找到自己的位置吧。

options.en: Let us sit in the nearest empty chairs and check our ticket numbers later.
options.zh: 先坐最近空椅，稍後再查票號吧。

options.en: Ask to reserve new seats before checking where the existing tickets already place us.
options.zh: 未查現有票已安排哪裏，就要求再留新位。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先按現有票號找已分配位置，可避免坐錯；先坐後查或未查就另留座，都未完成這項定位。

speaking.en: Could you help me find my seat using this row and number?
speaking.zh: 可否按這個行數及號碼，幫我找到位置？
speaking.promptZh: 你想具體提供座位資料並禮貌求助。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你回課室時，座位表已更新，舊位置有人用；你想按新表找自己的位置，而非直接選最近空椅。用一至兩句英文說明並求助。

examples.en: I need to find my seat on the updated classroom chart. Could you show me where my name is listed?
examples.zh: 我需按更新課室表找到自己的位置。可否指給我看名字列在哪裏？

examples.en: The seating plan has changed, so I will check the new chart to find my seat rather than assume the old place is still mine.
examples.zh: 座位表改了，所以我會查新表找自己的位置，而非假定舊位置仍屬於我。

writing.selfCheckZh: 交代座位安排更新，按新表定位或詢問；不把空椅、舊記憶或另作預留當已找到自己的位置。

takeaways.en: Please find your seat before the talk begins.
takeaways.zh: 講座開始前，請找到自己應坐的位置。

takeaways.en: We found our seats by matching the names on the table cards.
takeaways.zh: 我們對照桌上名卡，找到自己的位置。

sources.sentence: Sleeping early is easier said than done during exams.

brief.meaningEn: A suggestion sounds simple but is harder to carry out in practice.
brief.meaningZh: 建議聽來簡單，但實際做起來較難。
brief.grammar: That is easier said than done; doing something is easier said than done; identify the practical barrier.
brief.register: Conventional spoken contrast between a simple statement and its execution.
brief.boundaryZh: 不表示絕不可能，也不一定否定目標；可以承認困難後，提出可行小步。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能只用這句逃避所有行動，需說清甚麼限制令實踐較難。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出建議與實際條件的落差，並合作尋找下一步。

options.en: The goal sounds straightforward, but transcription creates practical work.
options.zh: 目標聽來直接，但轉錄帶來實際工作。

options.en: Most handwritten pages have already been transcribed because the search tool is ready.
options.zh: 因搜尋工具已備妥，大部分手寫頁也已轉錄。

options.en: The volunteers reject the aim entirely and do not intend to make any pages searchable.
options.zh: 義工完全否定目標，無意令任何頁可搜尋。

options.en: A working search tool means the handwriting will be searchable without anyone transcribing it.
options.zh: 有搜尋工具，就表示無需任何人轉錄，手寫內容也會可搜尋。

listening.explanationZh: 不少手寫頁仍需時間轉錄，是簡單目標與實際工作落差；不是工具可用就已多數轉錄、完全放棄，或無需轉錄。
listening.en: Making all the archive pages searchable is easier said than done: many are handwritten, and the volunteers still need time to transcribe them.
listening.zh: 把檔案每頁都做成可搜尋，說來容易做來難：不少是手寫頁，義工仍需時間轉錄。

reply.promptEn: Why can the volunteers not make every page searchable immediately?
reply.promptZh: 義工為甚麼不能立即令每頁都可搜尋？

options.en: Many handwritten pages still need to be transcribed.
options.zh: 不少手寫頁仍需轉錄。

options.en: It is easier said than done because the transcription takes time.
options.zh: 轉錄需時，所以說來容易做來難。

options.en: The suggestion leaves out the work needed to turn handwriting into usable text.
options.zh: 建議漏計了把手寫內容轉成可用文字的工作。

options.en: They need a practical plan for the handwritten material, not only the desired result.
options.zh: 他們需處理手寫材料的實際計劃，不只說想要的結果。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代轉錄限制，金句也給原因，不把困難當永久無望。

scene.promptZh: 朋友說「每天都約全組練習很簡單」，但各人更次不同，尚未找到共同時段。哪句貼切？

options.en: Meeting every day is easier said than done with those different shifts.
options.zh: 各人更次不同，每天見面說來容易做來難。

options.en: All members already share a confirmed daily rehearsal slot.
options.zh: 全體已確認有共同每日排練時段。

options.en: Different shifts do not matter, so the group can announce a shared time without comparing availability.
options.zh: 不同更次不重要，小組不比空檔也可宣布共同時段。

scene.explanationZh: 更次不同、尚無共同空檔，提供實踐限制；不是已確認時段，也不宜未比空檔就宣布。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜由 easier said than done 得出？

options.en: The suggested action has practical difficulties.
options.zh: 建議行動有實際困難。

options.en: The difficulty means the speaker has decided against trying the suggestion.
options.zh: 這項困難表示說話者已決定不試建議。

options.en: The speaker may need to explain the gap between the idea and the work required.
options.zh: 說話者可能需解釋想法與所需工作的落差。

contrast.explanationZh: 說明實踐較難，並未必已決定放棄；仍需了解限制及可能第一步。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴聽到轉錄需時，就想直接放棄整份檔案；你們可先處理最常查的頁面。哪句較好？

options.en: It is easier said than done, but we can start with the frequently used pages and estimate the rest of the work.
options.zh: 雖然說來容易做來難，但可先做常用頁，估餘下工作。

options.en: Declare the whole archive unusable before checking which pages people need most.
options.zh: 未查最需哪些頁，就宣告整份檔案無法用。

options.en: Announce that all pages are searchable now because the aim itself is clear.
options.zh: 只因目標清楚，就宣布現在每頁都可搜尋。

dialogue.explanationZh: 有困難仍可先做可行部分；不能把目標當成果，也不需未評估就全棄。

speaking.en: It is easier said than done, so let us identify the obstacle and choose a useful first step.
speaking.zh: 說來容易做來難，所以找出障礙，選有用的第一步吧。
speaking.promptZh: 你想承認實踐難度並提出合作行動。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你曾隨口取笑朋友的作品，現在知道令對方難過。旁人說「道歉不就行了」，但你擔心措辭再次傷人，想先寫下自己做錯甚麼，再真誠面談，不逃避責任。用一至兩句英文說明實踐難度及第一步。

examples.en: Apologising is easier said than done when I am afraid of choosing hurtful words again. I will first write down what I did wrong, then speak honestly to my friend.
examples.zh: 當我怕再說傷人的話，道歉便說來容易做來難。我會先寫下自己做錯甚麼，再真誠和朋友說。

examples.en: Repairing trust is easier said than done, but that is not a reason to avoid the conversation. I want to acknowledge my mistake without making excuses.
examples.zh: 修補信任說來容易做來難，但這不是逃避對話的理由。我想承認錯誤，不找藉口。

writing.selfCheckZh: 交代道歉措辭及受損信任的實踐難處，仍承認自己的行為、提出真誠第一步；較難不代表可以逃避或保證對方立即原諒。

takeaways.en: Keeping every appointment unchanged is easier said than done when shifts vary.
takeaways.zh: 更次有變時，要每個約見都不改，說來容易做來難。

takeaways.en: The plan was easier said than done, but a small trial helped us begin.
takeaways.zh: 計劃說來容易做來難，但小試驗幫我們開始。

sources.sentence: The walkers left at the crack of dawn.

brief.meaningEn: Very early in the morning, around the beginning of daylight.
brief.meaningZh: 非常早的早上，約在天剛亮之時。
brief.grammar: at the crack of dawn; fixed at + the crack of dawn; often a vivid approximate time description.
brief.register: Conventional dawn expression, not an exact universal clock reading.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是每天固定同一小時，也不表示一定比別人勤奮或更有價值；可為一次行程而早起。
brief.misconceptionZh: 需分開天亮時段與準確鐘點，不能憑這句替人物填上未交代的時間。
brief.outcomeZh: 能生動描述很早出發或開始，也保留時間資料精確度。

listening.promptZh: 這個表達交代甚麼時段？

options.en: Very early morning around the start of daylight.
options.zh: 天剛亮前後的大清早。

options.en: A fixed time of six o’clock in every place and season.
options.zh: 每個地方、季節都固定六點。

options.en: Late afternoon when the light is fading.
options.zh: 光線漸暗的傍晚。

options.en: The exact departure time, even though the sentence only gives the arrival period.
options.zh: 確切出發時間，即使句子只說到達時段。

listening.explanationZh: sky beginning to brighten 指黎明；片語不提供人人通用鐘點，也不直接給出發時間。
listening.en: We reached the hillside at the crack of dawn, just as the sky was beginning to brighten, so the photographer could watch the first light change.
listening.zh: 天剛開始亮時，我們大清早到山坡，好讓攝影者看最初光線變化。

reply.promptEn: When did you reach the hillside to see the first light?
reply.promptZh: 你們何時到山坡看最初光線？

options.en: We arrived just as the morning sky began to brighten.
options.zh: 我們在早上天空剛亮時到。

options.en: We got there at the crack of dawn.
options.zh: 我們在黎明大清早到。

options.en: It was very early, around the beginning of daylight.
options.zh: 很早，約在天剛亮時。

options.en: We reached the place before the brighter part of the morning.
options.zh: 我們在早上光線更亮那段之前到。

reply.explanationZh: 四句皆描述黎明時段，金句不硬填確切小時。

scene.promptZh: 故事中的送貨員在天空剛亮時開始首程，你想生動描述很早，而不填精確鐘點。哪句貼切？

options.en: The driver set off at the crack of dawn.
options.zh: 送貨員黎明大清早出發。

options.en: The driver began in the late afternoon as the sky darkened.
options.zh: 送貨員在天空漸暗的傍晚開始。

options.en: The phrase establishes the same six o’clock departure in every season.
options.zh: 片語確立每季都同樣六點出發。

scene.explanationZh: 天空剛亮與黎明相符，不等於傍晚或固定六點。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜由 at the crack of dawn 得出？

options.en: The event happened very early in the morning.
options.zh: 事情在大清早發生。

options.en: The exact same clock time applies wherever and whenever it happens.
options.zh: 不論何時何地，都套用同一確切鐘點。

options.en: A writer may still need a stated time if precision matters.
options.zh: 若要精準，作者仍可能需明示時間。

contrast.explanationZh: 黎明是時段，具體鐘點會依情境，不是通用固定小時。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友把「黎明到山坡」直接寫成「六點從家出發」，但未有路程或鐘點資料。哪句修改最好？

options.en: Keep at the crack of dawn as the arrival description, and do not invent an exact departure time.
options.zh: 保留黎明到達的描述，不編造確切出發時間。

options.en: Use a familiar morning hour as the departure time without checking how long the journey took.
options.zh: 不查路程需時，就用熟悉早上鐘點當出發時間。

options.en: Keep the arrival at dawn but report it as the time the travellers left home.
options.zh: 保留黎明時間，卻把它報作旅客離家的時間。

dialogue.explanationZh: 原文只給到達時段；不可改成確切出發鐘點，也不能把到達時段直接當離家時段，仍需路程資料。

speaking.en: We arrived at the crack of dawn, although the diary does not give an exact clock time.
speaking.zh: 我們黎明大清早到達，但日記沒有給確切鐘點。
speaking.promptZh: 你想保留生動時段而不捏造精確數字。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫虛構海邊村落的早晨，魚市場攤主在天剛亮時開門、放好空籃，街上還很安靜；你想描寫這個早段，不說每個地方都同一時間。用一至兩句英文描述。

examples.en: At the crack of dawn, the stallholders opened the fish market and set out empty baskets while the street was still quiet.
examples.zh: 黎明大清早，攤主打開魚市場、放好空籃，街上仍安靜。

examples.en: The fictional market began its day at the crack of dawn, with pale light appearing as people prepared the stalls.
examples.zh: 虛構市場在黎明大清早開始一天，人們備攤時，淡淡晨光出現。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以初現晨光及備攤描寫黎明，保留虛構場景；不把片語寫成全球固定鐘點或人物優劣判斷。

takeaways.en: At the crack of dawn, the first stallholder unlocked the market gate.
takeaways.zh: 黎明大清早，首位攤主打開市場閘門。

takeaways.en: At the crack of dawn, the village street was still quiet.
takeaways.zh: 黎明大清早，村落街道仍安靜。

sources.sentence: Young children often bounce out of bed on holidays.

brief.meaningEn: Get out of bed in a quick, lively and enthusiastic way.
brief.meaningZh: 以快速、活潑而有精神的方式起床。
brief.grammar: bounce out of bed; bounced and bouncing; bounce uses its energetic-movement sense, not necessarily repeated physical jumping.
brief.register: Natural energetic-motion collocation. Cambridge lists this bounce sense and an out-of-bed example, rather than a separate opaque idiom.
brief.boundaryZh: 描述當次起床方式，不保證整天精力充足、沒有煩惱或每次都這樣；也不等於必須真的彈跳。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不可只因早起就說精神奕奕，需有活潑或熱切動作線索。
brief.outcomeZh: 能生動描述人物起床的精神與動作，不把一次行為變成健康或性格定論。

listening.promptZh: bounce 在這裏增加甚麼感覺？

options.en: A lively, eager manner of getting up.
options.zh: 活潑、熱切的起床方式。

options.en: Getting up slowly and reluctantly without interest in the visit.
options.zh: 對探訪沒興趣，緩慢不願起床。

options.en: A guarantee that she will feel equally energetic throughout the whole day.
options.zh: 保證她全天都一樣精神。

options.en: Only the fact that she woke early, with nothing said about her manner.
options.zh: 只說她早醒，完全沒交代動作方式。

listening.explanationZh: 急着展示禮物支持活潑熱切，不能由此保證整天狀態。
listening.en: On the morning of the long-awaited visit, she bounced out of bed and hurried to show her brother the small gift she had made.
listening.zh: 期待已久的探訪那天早上，她精神奕奕地起床，急着把自己做的小禮物給兄弟看。

reply.promptEn: How did she get up on the morning of the visit?
reply.promptZh: 探訪那天早上，她怎樣起床？

options.en: She got up eagerly and moved quickly towards the day’s activity.
options.zh: 她熱切起床，很快投入當天活動。

options.en: She bounced out of bed, keen to show the gift she had made.
options.zh: 她精神奕奕起床，熱切想展示做好的禮物。

options.en: Her movements showed excitement rather than reluctance.
options.zh: 她的動作顯出興奮，而非不願。

options.en: She left the bed with a lively sense of anticipation.
options.zh: 她懷着活潑期待感離開床。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都描述當次熱切動作；金句不只說時間早。

scene.promptZh: 小說人物本來期待第一天去學畫，早上很快起來、滿臉笑容地收好畫簿。哪句貼切？

options.en: He bounced out of bed, excited about the art class.
options.zh: 他期待畫課，精神奕奕地起床。

options.en: He remained in bed and had no wish to get ready.
options.zh: 他留在床上，無意準備。

options.en: He rose early but moved with clear reluctance and no enthusiasm.
options.zh: 他雖早起，卻明顯不願、毫無熱情。

scene.explanationZh: 快速準備及笑容支持熱切起床；單早而不願不同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以單獨支持 bounced out of bed？

options.en: A person gets up with visible energy and eagerness.
options.zh: 一個人起床時，明顯有精神及熱切。

options.en: A clock shows an early hour, but the person is still lying down reluctantly.
options.zh: 鐘顯示很早，但當事人仍不願地躺着。

options.en: A narrator describes a lively movement from bed towards a much-anticipated activity.
options.zh: 敘事者描述人物活潑離床，準備期待已久的活動。

contrast.explanationZh: 時間早不等於精神奕奕，需動作及態度線索。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友因人物今天精神奕奕起床，就想寫她每一天都沒有疲倦。哪句較準確？

options.en: She bounced out of bed that morning; the story has not told us how she feels every day.
options.zh: 她那早上精神奕奕起床；故事未交代她每天的感受。

options.en: Use this one eager morning as the basis for describing every later day as equally energetic.
options.zh: 以這一個熱切早上，作往後每天都一樣精神的依據。

options.en: Delete the gift and visit details because getting up early alone explains her excitement.
options.zh: 刪去禮物及探訪細節，因單早起就解釋她的興奮。

dialogue.explanationZh: 當次動作不是永久狀態證據，期待事件才提供熱情線索。

speaking.en: She bounced out of bed that morning, eager to begin the day she had been looking forward to.
speaking.zh: 她那早上精神奕奕起床，熱切開始期待已久的一天。
speaking.promptZh: 你想描述特定一早的熱切動作。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫日記人物一天的情緒變化：早上盼望野餐，她熱切又迅速起床；後來下雨，行程取消，她感到失望。用一至兩句英文寫出早上的精神，不把它延伸成整天都開心。

examples.en: She bounced out of bed at the thought of the picnic, eager to pack her lunch. The later cancellation changed her mood completely.
examples.zh: 想到野餐，她精神奕奕地起床，熱切想裝午餐。後來取消行程，完全改變了心情。

examples.en: Although she bounced out of bed that morning, she felt disappointed when rain cancelled the picnic. Her lively start did not describe the whole day.
examples.zh: 雖然那早上她精神奕奕地起床，下雨令野餐取消時，她卻感到失望。活潑開場不能描述整天。

writing.selfCheckZh: 描寫早上熱切起床，亦交代後來取消帶來不同心情；同一天不同時段可有不同狀態，不把起床精神當整天保證。

takeaways.en: The children bounced out of bed when the special day arrived.
takeaways.zh: 特別日子到時，孩子們精神奕奕起床。

takeaways.en: I do not usually bounce out of bed, even when I wake early.
takeaways.zh: 即使早醒，我通常也不是精神奕奕地起床。

sources.sentence: The student spent Saturday catching up on sleep.

brief.meaningEn: Get extra sleep after having had less than wanted or needed earlier.
brief.meaningZh: 先前睡得不足後，多睡一些。
brief.grammar: catch up on sleep / my sleep / some sleep; caught is past; this is the extra-activity sense of catch up on.
brief.register: Everyday phrasal-verb collocation. It describes additional sleep, without guaranteeing a precise biological repayment or giving a sleep prescription.
brief.boundaryZh: 不等於追看消息，也不代表某個固定時數可完全抵銷所有影響；本課只描述人物所做及所說。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要有先前不足及後來多睡的情境，不把任何遲起都當補睡。
brief.outcomeZh: 能準確描述補睡意圖或行為，保留原因及結果的證據範圍。

options.en: Got additional sleep after a shorter night.
options.zh: 睡得較少一晚後，再多睡一些。

options.en: Stayed awake to read the news missed during the journey.
options.zh: 留醒追看旅途中錯過的新聞。

options.en: Used the free morning to rest quietly while staying awake, without getting additional sleep.
options.zh: 用空閒早上安靜休息，保持清醒，沒有多睡。

options.en: Rose early for a compulsory appointment rather than sleeping longer.
options.zh: 早起赴必須出席約見，而非多睡。

listening.explanationZh: 短睡一晚後實際多睡，是補睡；不是追新聞、清醒靜坐或赴早段必須約見。
listening.en: After the late journey left me with a short night, I spent part of the free morning catching up on sleep instead of beginning the optional errands immediately.
listening.zh: 深夜行程令那晚睡得少，翌日空閒早上，我用部分時間補睡，沒有立即開始非必要雜務。

reply.promptEn: Why did you leave the optional errands until later that morning?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼把非必要雜務留待那早上稍後？

options.en: The late journey meant I had slept less than usual.
options.zh: 深夜行程令我比平常睡得少。

options.en: I was catching up on sleep after the short night.
options.zh: 短睡那晚後，我在補睡。

options.en: I chose to use some of the free morning for additional rest.
options.zh: 我選用部分空閒早上多休息。

options.en: I wanted more sleep before turning to errands that could wait.
options.zh: 我想先多睡，再做可等的雜務。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均回應先前睡少與非必要事可延後的安排，不把它當每人固定作息。

scene.promptZh: 角色連夜趕完一次行程，之後沒有早段約見，睡得比平日長，說是補先前不足。哪句貼切？

options.en: She was catching up on sleep after the journey.
options.zh: 行程後，她在補睡。

options.en: She was catching up on the news while staying awake throughout the morning.
options.zh: 她整早留醒追新聞。

options.en: She followed her usual full night with no earlier shortage or extra sleep described.
options.zh: 她維持平常完整一夜，未描述先前不足或多睡。

scene.explanationZh: 先前不足、後來多睡，構成補睡語境；不只因晚起就推斷。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個推論不宜由 catching up on sleep 得出？

options.en: The person gets extra sleep after an earlier shortage.
options.zh: 當事人在先前不足後多睡。

options.en: Lying awake while postponing chores counts as catching up on sleep, even without additional sleep.
options.zh: 躺着清醒、延後雜務，即使沒多睡，也算補睡。

options.en: The surrounding account is needed to explain the particular routine.
options.zh: 需周邊敘述，解釋該次作息。

contrast.explanationZh: 補睡需要先前不足後的額外睡眠；只是延後雜務、清醒躺着，仍未是多睡。具體作息仍需看敘述。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友只因室友今天較晚起，就寫他在補睡；其實沒有先前睡少的資料。哪句追問較準確？

options.en: Was he catching up on sleep after a short night, or simply following his usual routine?
options.zh: 他是短睡一晚後補睡，還是只依平常作息？

options.en: Use the late hour alone as proof that he had missed sleep earlier.
options.zh: 單憑較晚時間，就證明他先前睡得少。

options.en: Describe him as reading the latest news because catch up always concerns information.
options.zh: 因 catch up 總關乎資訊，就寫他在追新聞。

dialogue.explanationZh: 需查先前不足及實際多睡，不能只看鐘點或把所有 catch up 固定成新聞。

speaking.en: I was catching up on sleep after the late journey, not catching up on the news.
speaking.zh: 深夜行程後，我在補睡，不是在追新聞。
speaking.promptZh: 你想分開同一動詞片語配不同名詞的意思。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：劇本人物前晚拍攝到很晚，睡得少，打算休假時補睡；本幕結束時假期尚未開始。用一至兩句英文報告她的意圖，不寫成已做了，也不承諾效果。

examples.en: She plans to catch up on sleep during her day off after the late filming session. The break has not started yet, so this is still her intention.
examples.zh: 深夜拍攝後，她計劃休假時補睡。休息尚未開始，所以仍只是意圖。

examples.en: After the short night, she hopes to catch up on some sleep when filming pauses. The scene ends before we see whether she does.
examples.zh: 短睡一晚後，她希望拍攝暫停時補睡一些。本幕結束時，我們還未看到她是否實行。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把先前短睡與補睡意圖相連，用 plans 或 hopes 保留尚未實行；不報作已補睡或保證固定效果。

takeaways.en: After the long journey, I wanted to catch up on some sleep.
takeaways.zh: 長途行程後，我想補睡一些。

takeaways.en: She spent part of her free morning catching up on sleep.
takeaways.zh: 她用部分空閒早上補睡。

sources.sentence: After a long conversation, the clock has run away with them.
sources.expression: the clock has run away with them

brief.meaningEn: Stop noticing how much time is passing while engaged in something.
brief.meaningZh: 投入某事期間，不再留意時間已過多少。
brief.grammar: lose track of time; lost in the past, losing in progress; object time specifies this application of lose track.
brief.register: Established natural idiom taught instead of presenting the source’s creative clock-personification as a standard fixed unit.
brief.boundaryZh: 不等於不知道如何看鐘，也不證明故意遲到；是否錯過安排需看實際時間及情況。
brief.misconceptionZh: 與主觀覺得時間快過相關，但這裏重點是當時沒留意流逝。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述漏留意時間及其後核對，不用編造時鐘損壞或人物動機。

options.en: Their attention stayed on the photographs rather than on the passing hour.
options.zh: 他們注意照片，沒留意時間流逝。

options.en: They had checked the closing time continuously and deliberately chosen to ignore it.
options.zh: 他們一直查關門時間，刻意選擇不理。

options.en: They mistook the earlier opening time for the closing time, rather than becoming absorbed in the pictures.
options.zh: 他們把較早開門時間誤當關門時間，而非投入照片。

options.en: They finished early because they were monitoring every stage of the visit.
options.zh: 他們監察參觀每階段，所以提早完成。

listening.explanationZh: only noticed when reminded 連到投入照片，支持沒留意時間流逝；不是一直知情而故意不理，或把開門時間讀錯。
listening.en: We lost track of time while comparing the old photographs and only noticed the hour when the caretaker reminded us that the room was closing.
listening.zh: 比較舊照片時，我們忘了時間，直到管理員提醒房間快關才留意鐘點。

reply.promptEn: Why did the caretaker’s closing reminder surprise you?
reply.promptZh: 管理員提醒快關門，為甚麼令你們驚訝？

options.en: We had been absorbed in comparing the photographs.
options.zh: 我們一直投入比較照片。

options.en: We had lost track of time while looking at them.
options.zh: 看照片時，我們忘了時間。

options.en: We had not noticed how much of the available period had passed.
options.zh: 我們沒察覺可用時段已過多少。

options.en: Our attention was on the pictures until someone drew it back to the hour.
options.zh: 直到有人提醒鐘點前，我們注意都在照片上。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都解釋投入及漏留意時間，不自行推斷故意不守規則。

scene.promptZh: 你專心把模型接好，放下工具時才發覺已過兩小時，原以為只一會。哪句貼切？

options.en: I lost track of time while building the model.
options.zh: 砌模型時，我忘了時間。

options.en: I kept a careful minute-by-minute record throughout the task.
options.zh: 整項工作中，我逐分鐘仔細記錄。

options.en: I saw every reminder and deliberately ignored the agreed deadline.
options.zh: 我看見每個提醒，刻意不理議定限期。

scene.explanationZh: 完成才驚覺已久，支持沒留意流逝；不同於一直監察或刻意忽略。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 lost track of time？

options.en: A person notices the hour only after being absorbed in a task.
options.zh: 投入工作後，當事人才留意時間。

options.en: A person watches the clock throughout and consciously follows each scheduled stage.
options.zh: 當事人全程看鐘，有意識跟每個排定階段。

options.en: Someone is surprised by how long a conversation has lasted.
options.zh: 某人驚訝對話已持續那麼久。

contrast.explanationZh: 全程有意識看時間，與漏留意不同；仍要看驚訝背後的注意情況。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想把「忘了時間」寫成「故意不理關門通知」，但故事只說提醒時才察覺。哪句較準確？

options.en: They lost track of time; the story does not establish that they knowingly ignored an earlier warning.
options.zh: 他們忘了時間；故事沒確立他們明知而不理先前警告。

options.en: Treat their surprise at the reminder as proof that they had read and rejected a previous warning.
options.zh: 把他們聽提醒時驚訝，當作早已讀過並拒絕先前警告的證據。

options.en: Describe a broken clock as the cause without checking whether any clock malfunction was mentioned.
options.zh: 未查有否提時鐘故障，就寫壞鐘是原因。

dialogue.explanationZh: 沒留意流逝不同於已知故犯；時鐘損壞也需證據，不能自行填因果。

speaking.en: I lost track of time while working, so I want to check the next commitment before I continue.
speaking.zh: 工作時我忘了時間，所以繼續前想先查下一項安排。
speaking.promptZh: 你想坦白注意情況，也核對後續安排。先聽，再說。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在家練習烹調新菜，專心調味及記錄步驟，放下筆才發現已到約好的視像聊天時間；你想承認自己沒留意，立即聯絡，而非怪責時鐘。用一至兩句英文說明。

examples.en: I lost track of time while testing the recipe and writing down the steps. I will contact my friend now rather than pretend I had been watching the clock.
examples.zh: 試食譜、寫步驟時，我忘了時間。我現在會聯絡朋友，而非假裝一直看鐘。

examples.en: Cooking absorbed my attention, and I lost track of time before our video chat. I need to check in with my friend straight away.
examples.zh: 烹調吸住我的注意，視像聊天前我忘了時間。我需立即聯絡朋友。

writing.selfCheckZh: 交代投入烹調而漏留意的過程及即時聯絡，不編造壞鐘，也不把沒留意變成明知而故犯。

takeaways.en: I lose track of time when I become absorbed in drawing.
takeaways.zh: 投入畫畫時，我會忘了時間。

takeaways.en: We lost track of time during the conversation and checked the next departure afterwards.
takeaways.zh: 談話時我們忘了時間，之後核對下一班出發。
